CRITICAL: this is ONE adult shown twice. The full-body photograph and close portrait MUST have the SAME PAIR OF EYES, with the SAME iris colour for each corresponding eye. Have the face look straight at the camera in BOTH panels, under the SAME soft neutral light, with no mirrored head, no head tilt, no shadow-induced colour shift. Copy the eye design consistently across panels. As in the real latest photograph, the viewer-left iris is muted cool steel blue; viewer-right is a closely related cool slate blue-grey, only subtly greyer. BOTH eyes remain cool blue/grey; neither iris has brown, amber, hazel, yellow or a coloured outer ring. The full-body dog's eyes must clearly retain that same blue/grey pair rather than both turning dark grey or brown. Do not make one eye vivid icy blue while the other becomes dull or brown. Crisp iris texture, dark natural pupils and subtle matching catchlights.
Preserve identity from the actual photos: copper-dominant muzzle and cheeks, copper brows, finely streaked silver/charcoal crown, grey folded ears with darker edges, dark irregular eyeliner. Preserve the small pale central nose-bridge detail at its observed extent; do not invent a broad white stripe. Black nose. Earlier photo supplies tan forelegs, short white toe tips and small dark leg/shoulder patches; no tall white boots. White chest bib. Hidden body and tail areas are plausible completion.
Composition: landscape 3:2 paired photographs, left about 60% a complete standing adult in a three-quarter flank body view with FRONT-FACING head, all four paws and entire tail comfortably visible; right about 40% a close FRONT-FACING face and upper chest of the IDENTICAL adult. Keep all face markings, ears, nose, and especially iris colours consistent between panels. Thin plain divider. Quiet outdoor grass/earth setting, neutral natural daylight and realistic fur detail. No basket, flowers, toys, person, collar or extra dogs.
Text: small white serif '01 · Copper face' at upper left, and 'AI concept · Appearance may vary' at lower right.
